questions.prompt: Which nutrient is the main source of energy in a meal based on ugali, rice or chapati?
options: Carbohydrate
Protein
Vitamin C
Calcium
questions.correctAnswer: Carbohydrate
questions.explanation: Cereal and starchy foods mainly supply carbohydrate, which the body uses for energy.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is most associated with preventing scurvy and helping wound healing?
options: Vitamin C
Vitamin A
Vitamin D
Vitamin K
questions.correctAnswer: Vitamin C
questions.explanation: Vitamin C supports collagen formation, healthy gums and healing of body tissues.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is needed in haemoglobin for oxygen transport in blood?
options: Iron
Iodine
Sodium
Fluoride
questions.correctAnswer: Iron
questions.explanation: Iron is part of haemoglobin, the blood pigment that carries oxygen around the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify mineral elements needed for healthy body functions.

questions.prompt: Which term describes illness caused by eating food contaminated with harmful microorganisms or toxins?

Food fortification
Meal planning
Food budgeting

questions.prompt: Which food preservation method removes most water from food to slow microbial growth?
options: Drying
Whisking
Peeling
Garnishing
questions.correctAnswer: Drying
questions.explanation: Drying reduces water available to microorganisms, so spoilage becomes slower.
questions.learningOutcome: Name preservation methods and the principles behind them.

questions.prompt: Which natural fibre is obtained from the flax plant?
options: Linen
Wool
Silk
Acrylic

questions.explanation: Linen is a plant fibre obtained from flax stems and is valued for strength and coolness.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sources of common textile fibres.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of pressing during garment construction?

To remove all fibre from fabric
To replace measuring before cutting
To make fabric permanently waterproof
questions.correctAnswer: To shape seams and give a neat finish
questions.explanation: Pressing controls seam allowances, sets construction details and improves garment appearance.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of pressing at different stages of garment construction.

questions.prompt: Which consumer document is normally issued after paying for goods or services?
options: Receipt
Pattern envelope
Menu plan
Care label
questions.correctAnswer: Receipt
questions.explanation: A receipt confirms payment and records key details of the transaction.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify documents used in everyday consumer transactions.

questions.prompt: Which household resource is classified as human rather than non-human?
options: Skill
Money
Land
Equipment
questions.correctAnswer: Skill
questions.explanation: Skill is a human resource because it belongs to people and affects how tasks are done.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify human and non-human resources used in family management.

questions.prompt: Which design element refers to the lightness or darkness of a colour?
options: Value
Texture
Line
Pattern
questions.correctAnswer: Value
questions.explanation: Value describes how light or dark a colour appears in a design scheme.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify elements of design used in interior arrangement.

questions.prompt: Which first-aid item is used to cover and protect a clean wound?
options: Sterile dressing
Detergent powder
Measuring tape
Tailor's chalk
questions.correctAnswer: Sterile dressing
questions.explanation: A sterile dressing protects a wound from dirt and reduces infection risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify first-aid materials used for common household injuries.

questions.prompt: Which term means the arrangement of furniture and equipment to support room function and movement?
options: Space planning
Food budgeting
Stain removal
Fabric blending
questions.correctAnswer: Space planning
questions.explanation: Space planning organizes room areas so people can use them safely and comfortably.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe basic terms used in planning household spaces.

questions.prompt: Why should adolescents include enough protein in their diet?
options: They need it for growth, tissue repair and body maintenance
It replaces all minerals in the body
It prevents the need for water
It turns every meal into a low-cost meal
questions.correctAnswer: They need it for growth, tissue repair and body maintenance
questions.explanation: Adolescence is a growth period, so protein supports new tissue formation and repair.
questions.subStrandTitle: Nutritional Needs Across the Life Cycle
questions.learningOutcome: Explain nutrient needs of adolescents and other family members.

questions.prompt: Which meal best provides energy, body-building and protective nutrients for a senior school learner?
options: Githeri with vegetables, avocado and clean water
Plain tea with sugar only
Soda and crisps only
White bread without any spread or fruit
questions.correctAnswer: Githeri with vegetables, avocado and clean water
questions.explanation: The meal combines carbohydrate, plant protein, vegetables, healthy fat and water.
questions.learningOutcome: Select balanced meals using locally available foods.

questions.prompt: Why is roughage important in the diet even though it is not digested for energy?
options: It adds bulk and helps normal bowel movement
It converts fat into vitamins
It kills all bacteria in food
It replaces the need for balanced meals
questions.correctAnswer: It adds bulk and helps normal bowel movement
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre supports digestion by helping food waste move through the intestines.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of fibre in healthy eating.

questions.prompt: Which cooking practice best conserves vitamin C in sukuma wiki?
options: Cook quickly in little water and serve soon
Boil for a long time in plenty of water
Cut and leave uncovered for many hours
Add baking soda to keep a bright colour
questions.correctAnswer: Cook quickly in little water and serve soon
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is easily lost through heat, water and air, so short cooking helps retain more of it.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply preparation methods that reduce nutrient loss in vegetables.

questions.prompt: Why should raw chicken and cooked rice be stored separately?
options: To prevent cross-contamination from raw food to ready-to-eat food
To make both foods taste sweeter
To reduce the need for refrigeration
To make cooked rice absorb more protein
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent cross-contamination from raw food to ready-to-eat food
questions.explanation: Raw poultry may carry harmful microorganisms that can contaminate cooked foods.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain practices that prevent contamination during food storage and preparation.

questions.prompt: Which sign suggests that fresh fish is of good quality?
options: Bright clear eyes and firm flesh
Strong sour smell
Slimy dull gills
Flesh that leaves a deep dent
questions.correctAnswer: Bright clear eyes and firm flesh
questions.explanation: Fresh fish usually has clear eyes, firm flesh, red gills and a mild smell.
questions.learningOutcome: Use quality signs when selecting perishable foods.

questions.prompt: Which storage condition is best for dry beans and cereals at home?
options: Clean, dry, covered containers away from pests
Open sacks on a damp floor
Containers mixed with detergent powder
Direct contact with leaking water pipes
questions.correctAnswer: Clean, dry, covered containers away from pests
questions.explanation: Dry covered storage protects foods from moisture, insects, rodents and dirt.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose suitable storage methods for common household foods.

questions.prompt: Why is blanching used before freezing some vegetables?
options: It slows enzyme action that can spoil colour, flavour and texture
It removes every nutrient before storage
It makes freezing unnecessary
It turns vegetables into fermented food
questions.correctAnswer: It slows enzyme action that can spoil colour, flavour and texture
questions.explanation: Brief heat treatment reduces enzyme activity so frozen vegetables keep better quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain preparatory steps used before freezing vegetables.

questions.prompt: Which condition helps yeast raise bread dough effectively?
options: Warmth, moisture and fermentable food
Very cold dry air only
Strong disinfectant in the dough
Complete absence of flour
questions.correctAnswer: Warmth, moisture and fermentable food
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugars in warm moist conditions and produces carbon dioxide that expands dough.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how yeast works as a biological raising agent.

questions.prompt: Which fabric property makes cotton comfortable in hot weather?
options: It absorbs moisture and allows air movement
It melts easily near heat
It never creases during wear
It is always waterproof
questions.correctAnswer: It absorbs moisture and allows air movement
questions.explanation: Cotton absorbs perspiration and can allow air circulation, which improves comfort in warm conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate fibre properties to comfort and fabric use.

questions.prompt: Why is a test seam useful before sewing a garment with unfamiliar fabric?
options: It helps check stitch length, tension and needle suitability
It replaces the need to cut fabric accurately
It removes all shrinking from the fabric
It changes synthetic fibres into natural fibres
questions.correctAnswer: It helps check stitch length, tension and needle suitability
questions.explanation: A test seam lets the sewer adjust machine settings before stitching the actual garment.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain steps used to prepare for quality machine stitching.

questions.prompt: Which choice is most suitable for an apron used during food practicals?
options: Durable washable fabric with comfortable fit
Fabric that melts quickly near heat
Loose net fabric that exposes clothing
Very delicate fabric that cannot be washed
questions.correctAnswer: Durable washable fabric with comfortable fit
questions.explanation: A practical apron should protect clothing, withstand washing and allow comfortable movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Select fabrics according to garment function and care needs.

questions.prompt: Why should laundry be sorted before washing?
options: To prevent colour transfer and choose suitable washing methods
To make all garments shrink equally
To remove the need for rinsing
To mix heavily soiled items with clean ones
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent colour transfer and choose suitable washing methods
questions.explanation: Sorting by colour, fabric and soil level protects garments and improves cleaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain reasons for sorting articles before laundering.

questions.prompt: Which stain-removal rule should be followed first for an unknown stain on a coloured fabric?
options: Test the remover on an inconspicuous area
Apply strong bleach immediately
Iron the stain to set it
Scrub hard with sand
questions.correctAnswer: Test the remover on an inconspicuous area
questions.explanation: Testing helps avoid colour loss or fabric damage before treating the visible stain.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe precautions when removing stains from fabrics.

questions.prompt: Why does a family prepare a budget before monthly shopping?
options: To match spending with income, needs and savings goals
To spend income without planning
To make every item more expensive
To avoid comparing prices
questions.correctAnswer: To match spending with income, needs and savings goals
questions.explanation: Budgeting helps families prioritise needs and control spending using available income.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of budgeting in household management.

questions.prompt: Which label information is most useful to a person avoiding peanuts?
options: Ingredient list and allergen warning
Package colour scheme
Advert slogan
Shelf position in the shop
questions.correctAnswer: Ingredient list and allergen warning
questions.explanation: Ingredients and allergen warnings help consumers avoid substances that can cause allergic reactions.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret product-label information for safe buying decisions.

questions.prompt: Why should a consumer compare unit prices when buying different pack sizes?
options: To know which pack gives better value for the same quantity
To choose the brightest package
To avoid reading the label
To increase packaging waste
questions.correctAnswer: To know which pack gives better value for the same quantity
questions.explanation: Unit pricing compares cost per standard amount, making different sizes easier to judge.
questions.learningOutcome: Use price information to make informed consumer choices.

questions.prompt: Which room arrangement best improves safety in a small living room?
options: Leave clear pathways between furniture pieces
Place stools across the doorway
Trail electric cables across walkways
Block windows with stacked boxes
questions.correctAnswer: Leave clear pathways between furniture pieces
questions.explanation: Clear movement paths reduce trips, allow access and make the room easier to use.
questions.learningOutcome: Arrange furniture to support safety and room function.

questions.prompt: Which colour choice can make a small dark room appear lighter?
options: Light colours with adequate lighting
Dark colours on every surface
No lighting and heavy curtains
Crowded dark furniture in all corners
questions.correctAnswer: Light colours with adequate lighting
questions.explanation: Light colours reflect more light and can make a small room seem more open.
questions.learningOutcome: Use colour and lighting principles to improve room appearance.

questions.prompt: Why should a kitchen have good ventilation?
options: To remove heat, steam, smoke and odours
To keep all food permanently fresh
To prevent any need for cleaning
To make cooking fuel unlimited
questions.correctAnswer: To remove heat, steam, smoke and odours
questions.explanation: Ventilation improves comfort and reduces indoor air pollution during cooking.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of ventilation in household rooms.

questions.prompt: Which practice saves household energy when cooking dry beans?
options: Soak the beans and cook with a lid
Keep the pot uncovered throughout
Start with dry beans and open the pot often
Use a very wide pot with little contact on the stove
questions.correctAnswer: Soak the beans and cook with a lid
questions.explanation: Soaking reduces cooking time and a lid limits heat loss.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply energy-saving practices in household food preparation.

questions.prompt: Which action follows the reduce, reuse and recycle approach most closely?
options: Use a clean container again before recycling it
Burn plastic waste behind the house
Buy disposable plates for daily meals
Mix broken glass with food scraps
questions.correctAnswer: Use a clean container again before recycling it
questions.explanation: Reuse extends the life of an item and recycling recovers materials after further use is not practical.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose sustainable ways of managing household waste.

questions.prompt: Which first-aid response is suitable for a minor steam burn?
options: Cool the area under clean running water
Apply cooking oil immediately
Break any blisters with a needle
Cover it with dirty cloth
questions.correctAnswer: Cool the area under clean running water
questions.explanation: Cooling a minor burn helps reduce heat damage and pain before further care is given.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe first-aid responses for minor household burns.

questions.prompt: Which value is shown when family members share household duties fairly?
options: Responsibility
Wastefulness
Neglect
Dishonesty
questions.correctAnswer: Responsibility
questions.explanation: Fair sharing of duties shows responsibility and supports cooperation in family life.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise values that promote harmonious family living.

questions.prompt: Which step is most sensible before starting a small home baking enterprise?
options: Find out customer needs, costs, hygiene rules and selling price
Bake large quantities before checking demand
Borrow money without a plan
Ignore packaging and food safety
questions.correctAnswer: Find out customer needs, costs, hygiene rules and selling price
questions.explanation: A simple feasibility check helps the enterprise meet demand safely and profitably.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify planning steps for a Home Science related enterprise.

questions.prompt: A meal of rice and cabbage is planned for lunch. Which addition best improves protein quality and overall balance?
options: Beans or lentils
More salt only
A bottle of soda
Extra cooking oil only
questions.correctAnswer: Beans or lentils
questions.explanation: Legumes add protein and minerals, making the meal more balanced than starch and vegetables alone.
questions.learningOutcome: Improve meals by adding locally available foods from missing food groups.

questions.prompt: A pregnant woman has low iron intake. Which meal choice best supports iron intake and absorption?
options: Beans, dark green vegetables and an orange
White rice with tea only
Cassava with soda
Plain mandazi with strong tea
questions.correctAnswer: Beans, dark green vegetables and an orange
questions.explanation: Beans and greens provide iron, while vitamin C from the orange improves absorption of plant iron.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan meals that meet increased nutrient needs during pregnancy.

questions.prompt: Why is frequent use of strong tea with iron-rich plant meals discouraged for a person at risk of anaemia?
options: Tea tannins can reduce absorption of non-haem iron
Tea turns iron into protein
Tea supplies all needed iron
Tea makes vegetables unsafe to eat
questions.correctAnswer: Tea tannins can reduce absorption of non-haem iron
questions.explanation: Tannins in tea can bind plant iron and lower the amount absorbed by the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors that affect absorption of nutrients from meals.

questions.prompt: A family wants to reduce hypertension risk through diet. Which change is most appropriate?
options: Use less salt and include fruits, vegetables and whole grains
Increase salty snacks and processed meats
Replace water with sugary drinks
Avoid all vegetables
questions.correctAnswer: Use less salt and include fruits, vegetables and whole grains
questions.explanation: Lower salt intake and more protective foods support healthier blood pressure control.
questions.learningOutcome: Adapt meals for common diet-related health conditions.

questions.prompt: Which menu is most suitable for a person managing diabetes during a school lunch?
options: Whole maize githeri, vegetables and unsweetened water
Soda, cake and sweets
White bread with jam and sweetened juice
Deep-fried potatoes with sugary tea
questions.correctAnswer: Whole maize githeri, vegetables and unsweetened water
questions.explanation: Whole foods with fibre and no added sugary drink help manage blood glucose better.
questions.learningOutcome: Select meal options suitable for people with diabetes.

questions.prompt: A recipe uses 250 g flour for 10 scones. How much flour is needed for 30 similar scones?
questions.explanation: Thirty scones are three times ten scones, so the flour is 250 g multiplied by 3.
questions.learningOutcome: Scale recipe quantities accurately for a required number of servings.

questions.prompt: A recipe serves 4 people and needs 600 ml milk. How much milk is needed for 6 people if portions stay the same?
options: 900 ml
750 ml
800 ml

questions.explanation: Six people are one and a half times four people, so 600 ml multiplied by 1.5 gives 900 ml.
questions.learningOutcome: Use proportion to adjust ingredients for different serving numbers.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches a preservation method with its main principle?
options: Salting - lowers water available to microorganisms
Freezing - adds warmth for microbial growth
Drying - increases food moisture
Canning - leaves food exposed to air
questions.correctAnswer: Salting - lowers water available to microorganisms
questions.explanation: Salt draws out water and reduces the moisture needed by many spoilage organisms.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate preservation methods to the scientific principles that make them work.

questions.prompt: Why are jars sterilised before filling them with jam?

To make the glass sweeter
To increase the fruit's water content
To remove the need for sugar and heat

questions.prompt: A learner fries mandazi in oil that is not hot enough. What result is most likely?

Leave it open on a dusty table

questions.explanation: Wrapping bread after cooling reduces moisture loss and protects it from contamination.

questions.prompt: Which fabric finish would be most useful for a tablecloth used in a school dining area?

The needle was kept in a needle case
The thread matched the fabric colour
The fabric was stored folded

questions.explanation: Uneven marking and measuring usually leads to an uneven finished hem.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify causes of common faults in garment finishing.

questions.prompt: Which seam finish is most suitable for fabric that frays easily?

Raw unfinished seam edges
Loose temporary tacking only
A fold with no stitching

questions.learningOutcome: Choose seam finishes that suit fabric behaviour and garment use.

Room colour scheme

Shopping receipt number

questions.learningOutcome: Diagnose common machine stitching faults and suggest remedies.

To make fabric edible
To replace all stitching
To remove colour from the garment

questions.explanation: Interfacing supports garment areas that need structure and resistance to stretching.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the functions of interfacing in garment construction.

questions.prompt: Which laundering method is safest for a woollen sweater labelled dry flat?
options: Gently wash if allowed, reshape and dry flat
Hang it dripping wet on a thin line
Boil it for a long time
Scrub it hard with a stiff brush
questions.correctAnswer: Gently wash if allowed, reshape and dry flat
questions.explanation: Drying flat helps wool keep its shape because hanging wet wool can stretch it.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply care-label instructions to maintain garment quality.

questions.prompt: A buyer compares rice packs: 2 kg at KES 320 and 5 kg at KES 750. Which pack is cheaper per kilogram?

The 2 kg pack

questions.learningOutcome: Calculate and compare unit prices for household purchases.

questions.prompt: A blender has a warranty but stops working after two weeks of normal use. Which action best protects the consumer's right to redress?
options: Take the receipt and warranty card to the seller or service centre
Throw away the appliance without reporting

Spread claims without checking warranty terms
questions.correctAnswer: Take the receipt and warranty card to the seller or service centre
questions.explanation: Proof of purchase and warranty information support repair, replacement or refund claims.
questions.learningOutcome: Use consumer records when seeking fair redress.

questions.prompt: Which advertising practice should make a consumer cautious?

Clear ingredient information
A visible expiry date
A fair comparison of pack sizes
questions.correctAnswer: A claim that sounds exaggerated and gives no evidence
questions.explanation: Unsupported exaggerated claims may mislead buyers and should be checked carefully.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate advertising messages before making purchases.

questions.prompt: A family has KES 1000 for supper ingredients. Which purchase best balances economy and nutrition?
options: Maize meal, beans, vegetables and fruit within the budget
All money spent on soft drinks
Only imported snacks for status

questions.correctAnswer: Maize meal, beans, vegetables and fruit within the budget

questions.prompt: Which kitchen layout principle improves workflow between storage, preparation and cooking?

Only dim decorative light behind the learner

A glaring bare bulb directly at eye level

questions.prompt: A wooden table has loose dust before polishing. Which cleaning method is most appropriate?

Scrub with coarse sand
Pour water and leave it standing
Use a knife to scrape the whole surface

questions.explanation: Gentle dusting removes loose dirt while protecting the wooden surface from scratches and soaking.

questions.prompt: Which time-management tool helps a family allocate duties and deadlines for cleaning day?

Food label
Warranty card
Fabric swatch

questions.prompt: Which home safety measure best reduces risk from electrical appliances in the kitchen?

Handle plugs with wet hands
Run cables through water on the floor
Repair damaged wires with paper
questions.correctAnswer: Keep cords dry and avoid overloading sockets
questions.explanation: Dry cords and properly loaded sockets reduce shock and fire hazards.

questions.prompt: Which response is most appropriate when a person inhales smoke from an indoor cooking fire?

Give more smoke to help them adapt
Make the person run immediately
Close all windows and doors
questions.correctAnswer: Move the person to fresh air and seek medical help if symptoms continue
questions.explanation: Fresh air reduces exposure, and ongoing breathing difficulty needs health care.

questions.prompt: A learner calculates that cupcakes cost KES 35 each to make and package. If selling at KES 50 each, what is the gross profit per cupcake?

KES 35
KES 50
KES 85

questions.prompt: A boarding student often skips breakfast and buys sweet snacks mid-morning. Which analysis best explains the likely effect?

Skipping breakfast always improves concentration
Sweet snacks supply all protective nutrients

questions.correctAnswer: Energy may rise briefly then fall, and nutrient intake may be poor
questions.explanation: Sugary snacks can give quick energy but do not provide balanced nutrients for sustained activity.

questions.prompt: A family eats mostly refined maize meal, tea and sugar. Which nutrient gap is most likely over time?

Excess protective nutrients

Complete nutritional balance

questions.learningOutcome: Identify nutrient gaps in common meal patterns and suggest improvements.

Only oily fried foods and no fluids
Stop all food until fully recovered
Give strong laxatives with every meal
questions.correctAnswer: Oral rehydration as advised, safe fluids and light nutritious meals
questions.explanation: Rehydration and safe easy-to-digest foods help recovery while preventing dehydration.
questions.learningOutcome: Adapt feeding practices to support recovery from common illnesses.

questions.prompt: A family wants to reduce nutrient loss when preparing vegetables for many guests. Which sequence is best?

Cut first, soak overnight and boil for one hour
Add baking soda and keep uncovered all day
Cook early in the morning and reheat many times
questions.correctAnswer: Wash before cutting, cut shortly before cooking and cook briefly
questions.explanation: This sequence limits nutrient loss through water, air, heat and repeated reheating.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate preparation sequences for nutrient retention.

Cook food early and leave it uncovered all day
Use one spoon for raw meat and salad
Allow visitors to handle food with unwashed hands
questions.correctAnswer: Keep hot foods hot, cold foods cold and use clean serving utensils

Mix it with fresh sauce to dilute it

questions.learningOutcome: Assess signs of unsafe preserved foods and choose safe actions.

questions.prompt: A cotton dress shrinks after the first wash. Which preventive action should have been taken before cutting?
options: Preshrink or launder the fabric as recommended
Cut the fabric without checking care needs
Use a hotter iron after sewing
Ignore the grainline completely
questions.correctAnswer: Preshrink or launder the fabric as recommended
questions.explanation: Preshrinking removes much of the initial shrinkage before garment pieces are cut.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse fabric preparation steps that prevent garment faults.

questions.prompt: A polyester blouse is uncomfortable during a hot practical lesson. Which fibre property best explains this?
options: Low absorbency can trap perspiration next to the skin
High absorbency keeps it permanently wet
It is an animal fibre with scales
It dissolves in ordinary wash water
questions.correctAnswer: Low absorbency can trap perspiration next to the skin
questions.explanation: Many polyester fabrics absorb little moisture, which can reduce comfort in heat.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how fibre properties affect comfort and garment performance.

questions.prompt: A seam puckers on a lightweight fabric after machine stitching. Which combined remedy is most appropriate?
options: Adjust tension, use a suitable needle and test stitch length
Pull the seam harder after stitching
Use a blunt needle and heavy thread
Skip pressing and trim all seam allowances away
questions.correctAnswer: Adjust tension, use a suitable needle and test stitch length
questions.explanation: Puckering often comes from unsuitable tension, needle, thread or stitch length for the fabric.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse stitching faults and select suitable remedies.

questions.prompt: A garment opening must lie flat, close securely and allow quick dressing. Which fastening choice is most suitable?
options: Zip fastener inserted neatly with reinforcement where needed
Temporary tacking stitches left in place
Loose decorative bow with no closure
Raw seam allowance without fastening
questions.correctAnswer: Zip fastener inserted neatly with reinforcement where needed
questions.explanation: A zip gives a secure, flat and quick-opening closure when inserted correctly.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate fastening choices for garment function and appearance.

questions.prompt: A label says wash separately in cold water. What risk is the manufacturer most likely warning about?
options: Dye bleeding or colour transfer
Permanent resistance to stains
Complete prevention of wrinkling
Improved fire safety
questions.correctAnswer: Dye bleeding or colour transfer
questions.explanation: Cold separate washing limits dye loss and protects other garments from colour transfer.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret care-label instructions and predict fabric-care risks.

questions.prompt: A family's weekly food budget is limited, but one member needs more calcium. Which buying plan is most realistic?
options: Include affordable calcium sources such as small fish eaten with bones, milk or fortified foods
Buy only costly imported snacks
Remove all protein foods to save money
Spend the whole budget on sweet drinks
questions.correctAnswer: Include affordable calcium sources such as small fish eaten with bones, milk or fortified foods
questions.explanation: Calcium needs can be met using locally available foods while still considering the budget.
questions.learningOutcome: Balance nutrition needs and cost when planning family purchases.

questions.prompt: A supermarket promotion says buy three, get one free for cooking oil. Which factor should a wise consumer check first?
options: Unit price, expiry date, storage space and actual need
Only the size of the poster
Whether the shelf is near the door
The colour of the bottle cap only
questions.correctAnswer: Unit price, expiry date, storage space and actual need
questions.explanation: A promotion saves money only if the unit cost, quality, storage and household need make sense.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate sales promotions before making buying decisions.

questions.prompt: A house has a kitchen opening directly into a poorly ventilated bedroom. Which concern is most important?
options: Smoke, heat and odours may affect health and comfort
The bedroom will automatically become bigger
The arrangement removes all fire risks
The kitchen will need no cleaning
questions.correctAnswer: Smoke, heat and odours may affect health and comfort
questions.explanation: Poor separation and ventilation can move cooking fumes and heat into sleeping areas.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse room relationships for safety, privacy and comfort.

questions.prompt: Which plan best applies universal design in a family bathroom used by children, adults and an elderly relative?
options: Non-slip floor, grab rail, good lighting and reachable storage
Glossy slippery tiles and no hand support
Storage only on a high shelf
A dark room with loose mats
questions.correctAnswer: Non-slip floor, grab rail, good lighting and reachable storage
questions.explanation: Universal design improves safety and accessibility for users with different abilities and ages.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate household spaces for accessibility and safety.

questions.prompt: A family keeps buying disposable plates for regular home meals. Which management issue is most evident?
options: Poor resource use because recurrent disposable purchases increase cost and waste
Excellent long-term economy
Complete elimination of household waste
A direct increase in food nutrients
questions.correctAnswer: Poor resource use because recurrent disposable purchases increase cost and waste
questions.explanation: Repeated disposables can raise expenses and waste compared with durable washable items.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse household choices for cost, convenience and environmental impact.

questions.prompt: A caregiver has four tasks: cook supper, help a child with homework, wash dishes and rest. Which approach best shows work simplification?
options: Combine compatible tasks safely, arrange tools nearby and share duties fairly
Do every task alone without a plan
Walk back and forth for each item
Delay all tasks until late night
questions.correctAnswer: Combine compatible tasks safely, arrange tools nearby and share duties fairly
questions.explanation: Work simplification reduces unnecessary effort while still completing tasks safely and fairly.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate methods of reducing time and energy use in household work.

questions.prompt: Which situation shows a priority need rather than a want in family spending?
options: Buying prescribed medicine for a sick family member
Buying a second decorative wall clock
Replacing working curtains for fashion only
Buying extra snacks after meals are already planned
questions.correctAnswer: Buying prescribed medicine for a sick family member
questions.explanation: Medicine for illness is a priority need because it protects health and wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish family spending priorities when resources are limited.

questions.prompt: A child swallows an unknown household chemical. Which response is safest?
options: Call emergency help or a poison centre and follow professional instructions
Force vomiting immediately in every case
Give kerosene to neutralise it
Wait silently to see what happens
questions.correctAnswer: Call emergency help or a poison centre and follow professional instructions
questions.explanation: Chemical poisoning needs urgent expert guidance because some actions can worsen injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe responses to household poisoning incidents.

questions.prompt: A home uses charcoal indoors with closed windows. Which risk is most serious?
options: Carbon monoxide and smoke exposure
Excess vitamin formation
Automatic food sterilisation
Improved air quality
questions.correctAnswer: Carbon monoxide and smoke exposure
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion in poorly ventilated spaces can produce dangerous carbon monoxide and smoke.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse health risks linked to household fuels and ventilation.

questions.prompt: A learner sells yoghurt at school without cooling facilities. Which risk should be addressed before continuing?
options: Bacterial growth in perishable dairy products
A guarantee of longer shelf life
Improved safety from warm storage
Loss of need for packaging
questions.correctAnswer: Bacterial growth in perishable dairy products
questions.explanation: Dairy foods are perishable and can become unsafe if held warm for too long.
questions.learningOutcome: Assess food safety requirements for small food enterprises.

questions.prompt: A small tailoring enterprise has many late orders. Which management action best addresses the problem?
options: Schedule orders realistically, track materials and communicate timelines
Accept every order without recording deadlines
Cut all garments before taking measurements
Stop checking quality to work faster
questions.correctAnswer: Schedule orders realistically, track materials and communicate timelines
questions.explanation: Planning capacity and materials helps meet customer deadlines without sacrificing quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse management practices that support reliable small enterprises.

questions.prompt: A snack business sells 40 packets at KES 60 each. Total variable cost is KES 1600 and packaging rent share is KES 300. What is the profit?
options: KES 500
KES 800
KES 2400
KES 1900
questions.correctAnswer: KES 500
questions.explanation: Sales are 40 multiplied by 60, which is KES 2400. Total costs are 1600 plus 300, leaving KES 500.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate profit after considering production and overhead costs.

questions.prompt: A school wants a one-week lunch menu for learners with different religions, allergies and budgets. Which planning principle is strongest?
options: Collect dietary restrictions, use varied affordable foods and label allergens clearly
Serve one dish daily and ignore restrictions
Choose only expensive imported foods
Avoid all protein foods to simplify cooking
questions.correctAnswer: Collect dietary restrictions, use varied affordable foods and label allergens clearly
questions.explanation: Inclusive menu planning considers health, culture, cost, variety and clear communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Design meal plans that balance nutrition, cost and diverse dietary needs.

questions.prompt: A community nutrition project wants to reduce iron-deficiency anaemia among adolescents. Which strategy is most complete?
options: Promote iron-rich foods, vitamin C pairings, deworming advice and reduced tea with meals
Advise learners to eat sugar only for quick energy
Focus only on attractive packaging of snacks
Ban all legumes from school meals
questions.correctAnswer: Promote iron-rich foods, vitamin C pairings, deworming advice and reduced tea with meals
questions.explanation: Anaemia prevention may need better intake, improved absorption and attention to health factors that reduce iron status.
questions.learningOutcome: Propose nutrition interventions for common adolescent health concerns.

questions.prompt: A food vendor wants to introduce dried mango slices. Which quality-control plan is best?
options: Use ripe sound fruit, hygienic slicing, controlled drying, moisture-proof packaging and date labels
Dry bruised fruit on dusty surfaces and pack while damp
Skip packaging so customers can touch samples freely
Add water after drying to increase weight
questions.correctAnswer: Use ripe sound fruit, hygienic slicing, controlled drying, moisture-proof packaging and date labels
questions.explanation: Safe dried products require good raw materials, hygienic handling, adequate drying and proper packaging information.
questions.learningOutcome: Design safe quality-control steps for preserved food products.

questions.prompt: A learner is developing a school uniform shirt. Which testing plan best checks fitness for purpose?
options: Assess fabric strength, comfort, colour fastness, seam quality, laundering response and cost
Check only whether the fabric has a bright colour
Ask one friend and skip measurements
Wash it once without inspecting seams or fit
questions.correctAnswer: Assess fabric strength, comfort, colour fastness, seam quality, laundering response and cost
questions.explanation: Uniforms need durability, comfort, good construction, manageable care and affordability.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop criteria for evaluating textile products for a defined use.

questions.prompt: A tailoring group wants to reduce fabric waste while cutting many aprons. Which approach is best?
options: Prepare accurate patterns, plan economical layout on grain and reuse suitable offcuts
Cut each apron randomly from the centre of the fabric
Ignore measurements and trim large pieces later
Dispose of all offcuts without sorting
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare accurate patterns, plan economical layout on grain and reuse suitable offcuts
questions.explanation: Careful pattern layout saves fabric while correct grain placement protects garment quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan garment construction processes that reduce waste and maintain quality.

questions.prompt: A family living room must support study, relaxation and visits in a small space. Which design solution is most effective?
options: Use zoning, multipurpose furniture, good lighting and clear circulation paths
Fill the room with large single-use furniture
Place study materials on the cooking stove
Block windows to create more wall space
questions.correctAnswer: Use zoning, multipurpose furniture, good lighting and clear circulation paths
questions.explanation: Zoning and multipurpose furniture help a small room serve several functions safely and comfortably.
questions.learningOutcome: Create interior arrangements that meet multiple household needs in limited space.

questions.prompt: A household wants to lower monthly utility costs without reducing hygiene. Which plan is best?
options: Fix leaks, use full laundry loads, improve ventilation, switch off unused appliances and monitor bills
Stop cleaning the home to save water
Leave appliances on so they are ready
Use more water because it feels cleaner
questions.correctAnswer: Fix leaks, use full laundry loads, improve ventilation, switch off unused appliances and monitor bills
questions.explanation: A combined conservation plan saves water and energy while still supporting cleanliness and comfort.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop practical plans for conserving household resources.

questions.prompt: A school Home Science room is being prepared for practical lessons. Which safety plan is most complete?
options: Clear walkways, labelled storage, first-aid kit, safe fuel use, hygiene rules and emergency contacts
Only decorate the room and ignore equipment checks
Store chemicals in food containers
Keep exits locked during practical lessons
questions.correctAnswer: Clear walkways, labelled storage, first-aid kit, safe fuel use, hygiene rules and emergency contacts
questions.explanation: A practical room needs prevention measures and response resources for food, fire, chemical and injury risks.
questions.learningOutcome: Design safety procedures for Home Science practical environments.

questions.prompt: A family conflict arises over unequal sharing of unpaid household work. Which response best supports fair family living?
options: Discuss tasks openly, consider each person's capacity and agree on a rotating schedule
Assign all tasks permanently to one person
Ignore the conflict until resentment grows
Reward only income-earning work and dismiss home tasks
questions.correctAnswer: Discuss tasks openly, consider each person's capacity and agree on a rotating schedule
questions.explanation: Open discussion and fair scheduling recognise household work and support cooperation.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop fair strategies for managing household roles and responsibilities.

questions.prompt: A learner plans to sell reusable fabric shopping bags. Which business plan element is most important before production begins?
options: Target customers, material cost, pricing, production time, quality standard and marketing channel
Only the learner's favourite fabric colour
A decision to sew without costing materials
A promise to sell without checking demand
questions.correctAnswer: Target customers, material cost, pricing, production time, quality standard and marketing channel
questions.explanation: A viable product plan links market demand, cost control, quality and sales strategy before resources are committed.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a basic plan for a sustainable Home Science enterprise product.
